text: Julesz also introduced a variant of the RDS called the anti-correlated random dot stereogram (ACRDS) [9] . Here, the luminance polarity of each element of the stereogram is reversed. Bright elements in the left eye's image are thus presented as dark elements in the right eye's image, and vice versa. Julesz showed that observers are able to perceive depth in correlated RDS (CRDS), but not ACRDS [9] .
source_label: Depth Perception Not Found in Human Observers for Static or Dynamic Anti-Correlated Random Dot Stereograms
